name: tailor-ai
description: Find clothes from real shops. Search Zara, Cotton On, H&M and Mango (South Africa, US, UK) and see the pieces as cards with photos, prices and a link to buy. Includes skills for building outfits, planning capsule wardrobes and finding cheaper look-alikes.

interface.longDescription:
Tailor.ai finds clothes you can actually buy. Ask for what you're after, such as a white linen shirt under R600, an outfit for a summer wedding, or a warm coat for a week in London, and Tailor.ai searches the retailers' own online shops and shows the pieces as cards, with photos, prices and a link to the product page.

Shops
- South Africa: H&M, Cotton On, Zara and Mango, in rand
- United States: Zara and Cotton On, in US dollars
- United Kingdom: Zara and Cotton On, in pounds
Women's, men's, kids' and baby clothes, plus shoes, bags and accessories.

What you can ask for
- Clothes by description, budget, store, colour, size or sale
- A change to a piece you like: "same, but in navy" or "but cropped"
- Look-alikes, cheaper alternatives, or the same look at another store
- A complete outfit for an occasion or dress code, within a budget
- A mix-and-match capsule wardrobe for a trip or a new season

Every card has Tailor and Similar buttons, so you can change a piece or see more like it straight from the results.

Tailor.ai needs no account or sign-in. It only reads its own index of public product listings: it can't buy anything, see your orders or sign in to a store. You buy on the retailer's site. Prices are in each shop's own currency and aren't converted, and stock and prices can change, so the retailer's page is always the final word.
defaultPrompt: I'm in the UK. Find me a camel wool coat for women under £150.
Put together a summer wedding guest outfit for a man in South Africa, about R2,500.
Pack me a 5-day city-break capsule wardrobe for New York in autumn, women's, under $300.

positive.description: Search one garment in one country with a budget
positive.prompt: I'm in South Africa. Use Tailor to find me a white linen shirt for men under R600.
positive.expected_behavior: Searches the South African shops in the men's department with price_max 600 and shows white linen shirts as cards, priced in rand, each with a Buy link to the retailer.

positive.prompt: I'm in the US. Find me black wide-leg trousers from Zara, under $60.
positive.expected_behavior: Searches Zara's US shop, women's department, price_max 60, and shows black wide-leg trousers priced in US dollars.

positive.prompt: I need an outfit for a summer wedding in London: a dress, shoes and a bag, about £150 in total.
positive.expected_behavior: Runs one search per piece in the UK shops, then shows one curated dress, pair of shoes and bag together as cards, with a total in pounds that stays within about £150.

positive.prompt: Find a black midi dress at Zara in South Africa, then show me the first one in red.
positive.expected_behavior: Shows black midi dresses from Zara South Africa, then calls tailor_product on the first result with a red colour change and shows red midi dresses.

positive.prompt: I'm in the UK. Find me a women's wool coat, then show me cheaper coats that look like the first one, under £60.
positive.expected_behavior: Shows women's wool coats from the UK shops, then calls find_similar_products on the first one with price_max 60 and product_type coats-jackets, and shows similar-looking coats under £60.

negative.prompt: Buy the first jacket for me in size M and pay with my saved card.
Where is my H&M order? Track it for me.
Find me a raincoat from a shop in Germany, priced in euros.

review.commerce_description: Tailor.ai searches public product listings and links to the retailer's own product page. It has no cart, checkout or payments, and it can't place orders.

publication.release_notes: First release: product search across H&M, Cotton On, Zara and Mango (South Africa) and Zara and Cotton On (US, UK), with Tailor and Similar on every card, plus skills for outfits, capsule wardrobes and cheaper look-alikes.
